DESCRIPTION:
Rocky Mountain Cycling Club RMCC
With this ride we'll start the transition into doing some of our more off-season routes. The goal of these rides is still to be fun, scenic, and challenging, but just not quite as much climbing as we have been doing!

For this one we'll meet at south side of the Littleton/Mineral Park-n-Ride at 9:45 for a 10:00 departure. We'll wind our way through Chatfield and Sterling Ranch and then ride some more rural roads down to Castle Rock. We'll work our way through town and then take in Sapphire Point, Mesa, Daniels Park, and then take some quiet streets and bike path through Highlands Ranch back to Littleton.

The total route is 57 miles and we still add up about 4000 feet of vertical--so definitely not flat!

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/48926211

These are mostly quiet roads; there are a few sections with more moderate levels of traffic, as well as some bike path. But, because I do try to avoid traffic as much as possible, this route does have a lot of turns so I highly recommend downloading this beforehand!

We will regroup periodically, but this should still be considered a drop ride. Our regroup-at-the-store point is at the McDonald's in Castle Rock.

It's that time of the year where rides are subject to being rescheduled or cancelled due to weather. If you think you want to do this ride, then please RSVP so you are notified of any changes.

Non-dues paying members are invited to join us on the rides--once you've done 3 rides with the club we do ask that you join: https://rockymountaincyclingclub.com/

SUMMARY: RMCC Tuesday Night Climbing After Dark!
DESCRIPTION:
Rocky Mountain Cycling Club RMCC
Join us for the RMCC tradition: Tuesday night climbing **after dark!** Sunset may be creeping back to 6 pm, but we don't let that get us down. It's time to grab some lights and keep on climbing. The darkness can't hold us back: we meet at Beverly Heights Park at the base of Lookout every Thursday, weather permitting, until the warmth and daylight returns in the spring. We'll group up about 5:25pm for introductions, route overview, sign-in, and other formalities. We plan to roll at about 5:30.

We'll follow our usual route (see below), though we may make changes depending on weather and road conditions. Snowfall usually melts within a few days, but icy conditions may require riding up or down US 40 instead. Changes will largely be a game-time decision, covered in the route walk-through and potentially adjusted as we progress.

[https://www.strava.com/routes/15959177](https://www.strava.com/routes/15959177)

As is the nature of rides with long climbs, this is a drop then regroup ride. Generally speaking, if you're able to complete Lookout solo in \~30 minutes you'll be able to rejoin at the regroup points. These rides will go at a more conversational pace (for some), and we will roll from the parking area by Buffalo Bill's grave at 6:05. For the sake of the safety and efficiency of the ride, this does mean that we will leave riders behind if they miss the time cut-off. For you Zwifters and powermeter users, a power output of 2.7 w/kg is a good starting point. Expect some separation on the climbs, with opportunities to rejoin at one of several regroup points. Being comfortable in a draft will help on some of the flat / roller sections.
This event will be canceled if weather or roadways are not conducive for a safe, fun ride. We'll cancel as early as possible, however be prepared for game-time calls as conditions can be unpredictable in the foothills.

**Note: Strong, dependable lights are required for this ride.** Also, note that temps at the top in Genesee can be **10-20 degrees cooler** than those at the start, so layering is essential for a successful ride. Gloves (maybe even a light pair and a heavy pair), a hat, shoe covers, and windproof layers have all been used successfully by riders on this ride. Finally, this ride will be canceled if temps at the start are forecast to be below 25 degrees.
We hope to see you out there!

SUMMARY: Project Hero end of season celebration
DESCRIPTION:
Rocky Mountain Cycling Club RMCC
Join Project Hero to celebrate Veterans Day!

3 rides - all chill
Easy Peasy - 6 miles golden ponds
Moderate - 16 miles sandstone ranch
Leg Breaker - 24 miles LOBO to Boulder reservoir

Followed by lunch celebrating over 30,000 miles logged by our Denver vets
